props.name: heading
props.description: Heading text for the alert, rendered as a `<span>`.  Named `heading`, not `title`, for the reason sk-card records: `title` is a standardized `HTMLElement` member and a prop by that name is shadowed by the prototype property, so the browser would surface it as a hover tooltip on the whole alert.  A string rather than a heading element: the alert does not know what level it sits at in the document's outline, and a hard-coded heading inside it produces a level that may contradict the surrounding structure. A consumer who needs a real heading puts one in the body itself.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual emphasis.  Only `variant` is an appearance prop. The variant also picks the component's default live-region role, unless the consumer has already set one.

ai.summary: An inline message about the current page: a success, a warning, a failure, or a note.
whenToUse: A result or a state needs stating next to the content it describes
A page-level or form-level failure must be visible without a modal
The message may need an action, such as Retry or View logs
whenNotToUse: It interrupts a flow the user must acknowledge — use an Alert Dialog
It is a transient, self-dismissing update — use a Toast
It labels a value with one word's worth of state — use a Badge
ai.accessibility: Carries `role="alert"` for the danger and warning variants, so those interrupt; the rest are `role="status"` and wait for a pause. The variant glyph is aria-hidden and differs in shape as well as colour, so the message survives a monochrome display. A consumer-set `role` is never overwritten.
ai.example: <sk-alert variant="warning" heading="Quota nearly full">Your workspace is using 96% of its quota.</sk-alert>
knownLimitations: No dismiss control, deliberately: a dismissible alert needs focus management and a close affordance that belongs to a Dialog or a Toast
The actions slot is not part of the announced message, so an action the user must take also needs to exist in the page
